title: Love God, Serve Man -- Ch. 20: Some Prayers and Invocations
keywords: National Day of Prayer and Renewal
Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting
primary_topics: Chapter 20 of 'Love God, Serve Man' -- a set of four public prayers and invocations CJP delivered between December 1991 and June 1994, showing how he adapted a single devotional idiom to a national prayer rally, two Rotary luncheons and a bishop's book launching

The family prayer at the first National Day of Prayer and Renewal (Rizal Park, December 14, 1991), asking God to show the nation 'the pivotal role of strong families in shaping a strong society' and that peace in the home is 'the lasting basis of genuine peace and harmony in the world'

The Rotary invocations (June 9, 1994 and July 29, 1993), each built on a 'we thank You... but we ask You even more' structure that accepts a material blessing and then asks for its spiritual counterpart -- electric power against ignorance, money's purchases against 'the things that money cannot buy'

The invocation at the launching of Bishop Teodoro C. Bacani Jr.'s 'Church in Politics' (January 16, 1992), a prayer for electoral reform pitting 'guns, goons and gold' against 'grace, gospel and God' and 'patronage, payoff and personalities' against 'principles, platform and prayers'
sub_topics: The editor's note frames the chapter: CJP was often invited to pray publicly at retreats and prayer meetings and to deliver invocations before civic and professional organizations, and these are four samples
Prayer 1 (Rizal Park, December 14, 1991) addresses 'God and Father of all families on earth' and asks that families see the urgency of praying 'in unity as one people and one nation'

It grounds national peace in domestic peace -- peace and harmony in homes as 'the lasting basis of genuine peace and harmony in the world' -- and ends on the image of families who pray together becoming 'living stones in building a society'

Prayer 2 (Rotary Club of Manila, Manila Hotel, June 9, 1994) opens by asking forgiveness for having focused on 'our weaknesses, afflictions and failures rather than on Your dominion, healing power and love for us'
It blesses the guest speaker, former Vice President Salvador H. Laurel, asking that he be anointed as he articulates 'his vision of a country transformed and a people renewed in Your Spirit'

It then runs its signature antitheses: thanks for electric power 'at long last' but a greater plea for 'divine power to free our minds from the darkness of ignorance, sophistry and self-righteousness'; thanks for the freedoms used on behalf of East Timor but a greater plea for zeal for 'our own people's liberation from hunger, injustice, poverty and disease'; thanks for what money buys but a greater plea for 'integrity, discipline, honor, hard work and faith in God'; thanks for temporal prosperity but a longing for eternal peace in the life hereafter

Prayer 3 (Villa San Miguel, Mandaluyong, January 16, 1992) thanks God for inspiring Bishop Bacani to write 'Church in Politics,' a book needed to let the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting transform political life as 'an indispensable part of their integral or total development as Christians'

It casts electoral work as spiritual combat -- 'we go into battle in Your political vineyard' -- asking courage to defeat 'guns, goons and gold,' the 'politics of patronage, payoff and personalities,' and to elect officials who are 'Maka-Diyos, Maka-Bayan, Maka-Tao at Maka-Mahirap'

Prayer 4 (Rotary Club of Manila, Manila Hotel Fiesta Pavilion, July 29, 1993) proclaims God's presence 'amongst us.. around us. within us' in a chain of participles -- molding, teaching, inspiring, empowering, healing and leading

It asks 'peace and prosperity for our land, sagacity and integrity for our leaders, dignity and solidarity for our people,' and a community 'where the weak shall be strong and the strong shall be just and the just shall be compassionate'
It closes by asking a special outpouring of grace on the guest speaker, Executive Secretary Teofisto Guingona Jr., that his words be 'the prophetic message that You would want us to hear and to heed'
All four prayers close in the same trinitarian formula -- through Jesus 'who lives and rules with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, forever and ever'

stances.rhetorical_move: petitionary anaphora ('Help us to know... Help us to see... Help us to realize') that builds from household to nation to world

stances.claim: Material blessings are real but subordinate: electric power, freedoms, possessions and prosperity should be received with thanks and then surpassed by requests for enlightenment, justice, integrity and eternal life.
stances.rhetorical_move: concessive antithesis repeated four times ('we thank You... but we ask You even more ardently/fervently/intensely'), each pairing a temporal gift with its spiritual counterpart

stances.rhetorical_move: alliterative opposition of vice-triads and virtue-triads, framed as a battle 'in Your political vineyard'

notable_anecdotes: Praying for the nation at the Luneta: his first prayer was delivered before families gathered at the Rizal Park grandstand for the country's first National Day of Prayer and Renewal on December 14, 1991.

Electric power and divine power: at a 1994 Rotary luncheon he thanked God for finally giving the country 'enough electric power to move our industries, light our homes and air-condition our offices' and asked more ardently for power against ignorance and sophistry.

East Timor and home: in the same invocation he thanked God for the freedoms used to work for the rights of the people of East Timor while praying 'even more fervently' for zeal on behalf of Filipinos' own liberation from hunger and poverty.
Praying at the Cardinal's residence: he gave the invocation for Bishop Bacani's 'Church in Politics' at Villa San Miguel, Jaime Cardinal Sin's residence, on January 16, 1992.

Blessing the speaker: twice he asked God to anoint the guest of honor -- Salvador H. Laurel in 1994 and Executive Secretary Teofisto Guingona Jr. in 1993, that his words be 'the prophetic message' the audience should heed.

one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 20 of 'Love God, Serve Man' collects four public prayers and invocations Artemio V. Panganiban delivered between December 1991 and June 1994, introduced by an editor's note observing that he was often invited to pray at retreats and prayer meetings and to give invocations before civic and professional organizations. The first, at the country's first National Day of Prayer and Renewal at the Rizal Park grandstand on December 14, 1991, addressed 'God and Father of all families on earth' and asked that families grasp the need to pray 'in unity as one people and one nation,' see 'the pivotal role of strong families in shaping a strong society,' and recognize peace in the home as 'the lasting basis of genuine peace and harmony in the world,' ending on the image that 'when families pray together, they stay together and become living stones in building a society.' The second, before the Rotary Club of Manila at the Manila Hotel on June 9, 1994, asked forgiveness for dwelling on weakness rather than on God's healing power, blessed guest speaker Salvador H. Laurel, and then ran a fourfold antithesis: thanks for electric power at last, but a greater plea for 'divine power to free our minds from the darkness of ignorance, sophistry and self-righteousness'; thanks for the freedoms used for the people of East Timor, but a greater plea for zeal for Filipinos' own liberation from hunger and poverty; thanks for what money buys, but a greater plea for 'integrity, discipline, honor, hard work and faith in God'; thanks for prosperity, but a longing for eternal peace hereafter. The third, at the launching of Bishop Teodoro C. Bacani Jr.'s 'Church in Politics' at Villa San Miguel on January 16, 1992, thanked God for the book that would let the Parish Pastoral Council for Responsible Voting transform political life, and asked courage 'to combat the evils of guns, goons and gold' and uphold 'grace, gospel and God,' to defeat the 'politics of patronage, payoff and personalities' in favor of 'principles, platform and prayers,' and to elect leaders who are 'Maka-Diyos, Maka-Bayan, Maka-Tao at Maka-Mahirap.' The fourth, again before the Rotary Club of Manila on July 29, 1993, proclaimed God's presence molding, teaching, inspiring, empowering and healing those gathered, asked for 'sagacity and integrity for our leaders' and a community 'where the weak shall be strong and the strong shall be just and the just shall be compassionate,' and sought a special outpouring of grace on guest speaker Executive Secretary Teofisto Guingona Jr. All four close through Jesus, who 'lives and rules with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God forever and ever.'
